chapters.title: One note too many
panels: The Ground's little bell rings once at closing, then rings again from an empty courtyard.
Mira checks the rope. It is tied in the usual knot.
A paper square under the bell reads: listen after the sound.
Dev hears a soft rattle when the second ring fades.
They find a loose bead inside the wooden bell frame.
The bead matches the blue curtain near the practice stage.
On Sunday, they lift the curtain. Behind it sits a box of old performance cards, all blank except one.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals a small drawing of three bells on the card.

chapters.title: The blank cards
panels: The marked card names a game once played at the Ground's annual fair.
Three bells gave three clues; the first team to listen closely won a sweet.
The fair book lists the game but omits the winning team.
Mira asks the sweet seller, who remembers a group that shared the prize.
Their names are pencilled on a wrapper inside the card box.
One name is crossed out so neatly it looks like a line in the design.
On Sunday, the crossed-out name resolves under angled light. It belongs to the person who wrote the fair book.
chapters.bonus: The bonus panel shows a note: 'I wanted everyone to win.'

chapters.title: A fairer game
panels: The writer says the old game rewarded speed more than care.
She crossed out her name when she redesigned it for teams to share clues.
The second bell was her invitation to try the new version.
Mira sets out three blank cards for the next fair.
Dev draws a bell, a window and a cup on them.
Visitors solve each clue by talking to someone they have not met.
On Sunday, the final card is missing. In its place sits a cup of tea, still warm.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals a card tucked beneath the saucer.

chapters.title: Tea for the finder
panels: The card beneath the cup says: find the person who remembers the first bell.
The oldest caretaker says the bell came from a railway waiting room.
It was given when that room closed, to keep its welcome alive.
Mira looks for the gift record and finds a drawing instead.
The drawing shows a small shelf beside the bell for visitors' notes.
The shelf was never built because nobody could agree where it belonged.
On Sunday, they choose the courtyard wall. A hidden pencil mark on the drawing matches a mark already there.
chapters.bonus: The bonus panel reveals the marks were made by the same carpenter years apart.

chapters.title: After the bell
panels: The carpenter makes the shelf from wood left after the reading benches.
Mira leaves the first blank card on it, with a pencil on a string.
A child writes: 'I heard the rain stop.'
Someone else adds: 'I noticed the person who held the gate.'
The bell rings once at closing. This time everyone waits for the quiet after it.
In that quiet, Dev hears pages turning and a few people laughing softly.
On Sunday, the shelf is full. The last card asks a new question: what will we notice next season?
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals an empty card ready for the player's own answer.
